notes:
`PRODUCT_VERSION` 1.3.0 · `CONTRACT_VERSION` 4.5.0

1.3.0 is about teams sharing a brain. A machine holds several licenses, each its own context, and a team's knowledge can live on a gateway hosted by toryo or, on Enterprise, by the team. Projects are shared by git remote, knowledge moves into a team as bundles, and `code-task` routes implement by work class under a spend guard. Upgrade gateways before seats; upgrading moves no existing data.

### Added

- **Several licenses on one machine, each its own context.** `toryo license add`, `list` and `remove` keep more than one license beside the default, and a team seat's check-in also stores the holder's personal context. Every machine also has a local context that is always present, where unbound work and global knowledge land. `TORYO_CONTEXT`, or `--context` on the commands that take it, selects a context. Without either, the knowledge CLIs and operator MCP sessions use the context of the project the working directory is bound to. Runs, jobs, schedules and ideas are stamped with a `contextId` and can be listed by it, and a dispatched worker runs in its job's context. A job whose context does not verify fails before launch and is never run as the default instead. `license list` and `status` show a team's hosting mode and the seat's signed role.
- **Team knowledge lives on a gateway.** In a context hosted by toryo or self-hosted, knowledge commands go to the team's gateway over `POST /cli`, using the CLI contract as the wire format. The seat embeds locally and sends its vectors with the request. The gateway serves reads and writes inside its own process on pooled connections, spawns nothing, and asks a busy client to retry through `Retry-After`. It activates with its own gateway key and admits only seats of the team it serves. Global knowledge stays personal: a global memory written from a team context lands pending in the personal store, and board routes the notice to Memory review.
- **Projects can be shared across a team.** A project carries its git remote and subpath, and its root is now a binding local to each machine. A team identifies its shared definitions by remote plus subpath. Owners and admins add, update and remove them through the gateway, and a removal leaves a tombstone. `project bind --auto` binds a checkout to every definition its remote matches. `toryo project share` moves a local project into a team: it merges the project into the team's definition or creates one, moves its knowledge and execution records, and binds the checkout. A remote context's code index is built from the remote default branch and shared by every seat.
- **Seats have roles.** A seat is an owner, an admin or a member. Members cannot write shared definitions. Admins can run the owner-only project verbs and the portal's seat actions, but not billing, hosting or the gateway key. A demoted owner loses the owner-only verbs at the gateway within a day.
- **Knowledge moves between contexts.** `toryo knowledge export` and `import` carry memories and documents as a bundle, with vectors and embed scheme included, and import re-embeds when the scheme differs. `toryo license adopt` brings what an unlicensed install built into the licensed context. `toryo knowledge move-runtime` switches between docker and pglite and copies the execution databases and usage signals too. When an all-local team switches its hosting, `toryo knowledge move-hosting` moves this machine's part onto the gateway, and an hourly job finishes the move. Moves go one way, into a team, except that an all-local team's knowledge can come back to this machine's local context. `restamp` re-points execution records when a project merges or moves.
- **The Enterprise plan, and self-hosting.** Enterprise is a team plan that can self-host its gateway. The compose bundle and the gateway image ship as release assets, linked from a new Self-hosting page in the portal for Enterprise owners and admins. The portal also gains a Projects page for managing a hosted team's shared definitions, and a Knowledge page showing its usage counts.
- **`code-task` routes implement by the kind of work.** The planner declares a work class, `mechanical`, `standard` or `design`. A mechanical plan runs on a cheaper route with batched edits and a mechanical proof. A project can store an implement routing table (`toryo-project routing`), including which harnesses each class may use. It can also store model and effort defaults for code-task's other pinned roles (`toryo-project roles`), with a host-wide setting underneath. The plan gate gains a route section with selects for class, harness and effort, preselected from the route. A live preview shows the route, the estimate, each harness's quota and the spend guard for whatever is picked. claude accepts `max` effort.
- **Spend is guarded, and quota is routed around.** The plan gate shows an estimate of implement's cost. When a pass crosses its ceiling, a spend guard pauses it and asks whether to continue. When implement's harness is held at admission, dispatch moves the job onto the first allowed fallback that is ready and records the reroute on the job.
- **Runs report what they cost and what they did.** Every finished job records its harness, the model that actually ran, whether its cost was reported or estimated, its turns and its tool mix. `runs` and `status` carry a usage rollup, and a board-wide setting picks cost, tokens, turns or worker time as the figure to show. `toryo-sequence outcomes` prints one outcome row per finished run. `tool-usage` counts the code tools each step called, and `code-task` records the size of the diff it merged.
- **Code search sees more.** `toryo-code-index map` and the `code_map` MCP tool return a ranked repo map within a character budget. Search also matches full text over symbol names and doc comments. With `--worktree`, `search`, `map`, `file`, `exporters` and `importers` answer from a checkout laid over the index, uncommitted edits included. `brain_search` and operator sessions in a linked worktree do the same.
- **Sequence gates can carry forms.** A human gate may declare a `form:` of selects, text fields, numbers and toggles. It may also declare a `preview:`, which runs sandboxed code over the form's values. `toryo-sequence gate-form` renders both. A select can narrow its options from run state or from another field's value.
- **Board follows contexts.** Every brain screen has a context selector, and "All contexts" reads across all of them. Runs, jobs, schedules and ideas are labelled and filtered by context. Local projects offer Make team project and Sync to team. You can message the worker from a run's detail, and the Dev Tools screen restarts stale services.
- **`foreman doctor` names a stale install.** A new `workspace-install` check fails when a source checkout's install predates a merge that added a workspace dependency. Sibling CLIs now tell you to run `bun install` in that case, where they used to fail on module resolution.

### Changed

- **Self-hosting is Enterprise-only.** The license service refuses to make a Team-plan team self-hosted or to issue it a gateway key. A team already self-hosting on the Team plan keeps working.
- **Upgrading moves no existing data.** Global rows already in a team store stay there until `toryo-memory drain-global` runs in that context, and projects and bindings created in a team because it was the default stay in it (`docs/session-context.md`).
- **Upgrade gateways before seats.** Several of these changes sign or send something an older gateway cannot read: the seat role, seat-embedded vectors, the embed scheme and the bundle verbs. An older build reads Enterprise as not a team at all, so every seat and self-hosted gateway of a tenant must run 1.3.0 before that tenant moves to Enterprise.
- **Gateway configuration changed.** `TORYO_GATEWAY_CLI_CONCURRENCY` is retired, and `POST /cli` no longer answers 429. `TORYO_GATEWAY_DB_POOL_SIZE` now sizes the pool for each knowledge database separately, so a gateway can hold up to twice that many connections. A compiled `toryo-brain serve` refuses `--auth-disabled`, and `BRAIN_LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY` is no longer read.
- **`maxSubagents` also limits claude Workflow agents.**
- **MCP `sequence_status` returns a summary by default.** Pass `detail: 'full'` for the old shape; for a finished `code-task` it had grown larger than one tool result can carry. `sequence runs --project` accepts a slug.
- **The `move-runtime` summary reports each execution database table by table**, replacing `{moved: false, databases}`.

### Fixed

- **Acceptance reinstalls the worktree before its commands**, so a dependency the branch gained after the worktree was installed no longer fails as a missing module. The base check no longer blames a per-test timeout on the base branch.
- **`toryo setup`, `update` and `move-runtime` always migrate this machine's own stores**, whatever context the calling shell or session has selected.
- **The janitor no longer reaps a tmux session that is still launching.** A claude run whose pane was signalled or disappeared now ends instead of hanging.
- **The scheduler reports an unreachable gateway once per outage.** It also decays memory and schedules code-index jobs in every local context, not only the default.
- **`foreman check` reads stale code only from each service's own dependency paths.**
